original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. A gate job stands up the disclosure fixturenet from the warm snapshot, runs the Aave-yield disclosure example, builds a disclosure package, checks the hops, and tears down the fixturenet on exit. The user shields USDC, funds a channel with depositFromNote, earns yield as waUSDC, closes to a payout note, and unshields to a second account. The armada-disclosure-acceptance.py checker runs on the package and reports that hops H1, H2, H4, H5, H6, and H7 succeed. The second account gains a positive USDC amount. The two accounts differ. The payout note belongs to the same wallet. The package file path is not empty. The gate leaves no running fixturenet deployment after it exits.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. No disclosure hops gate job exists. No gate runs the Aave-yield disclosure example on the warm snapshot, checks the hops, and tears the fixturenet down.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-acceptance.py on the warm snapshot. exit_code is 0. stdout_json hops_ok is true. stdout_json eoa2_usdc_delta is greater than 0. stdout_json eoa_distinct is true. stdout_json payout_note_owned is true. stdout_json package_path is not empty. After the gate exits no disclosure deployment runs and the deployment directory is gone.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. The gate tears down its fixturenet with an exit trap. The gate removes the deployment directory on exit. The gate stands up the fixturenet from the warm snapshot, not from a cold build.
restatement: A new gate job must prove the Aave-yield disclosure flow end to end on the disclosure fixturenet. The gate stands up the fixturenet from the warm snapshot, not from a cold build. It runs the Aave-yield disclosure example: the user shields USDC, funds a channel with depositFromNote, earns yield as waUSDC, closes to a payout note, and unshields to a second account. It builds a disclosure package and runs stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-acceptance.py on it. The checker must exit 0 and report hops_ok true, so hops H1, H2, H4, H5, H6 and H7 succeed. It must report eoa2_usdc_delta greater than 0, eoa_distinct true, payout_note_owned true, and a non-empty package_path. The gate tears down the fixturenet through an exit trap and removes the deployment directory, so no disclosure deployment runs after the gate exits.

restatement_clauses.text: A disclosure hops gate job exists as the gate script env/gates/nitro-e2e/disclosure-hops.sh.
The gate stands up the fixturenet from the warm snapshot, not from a cold build.
The gate tears down its fixturenet with an exit trap.
The gate removes the deployment directory on exit.
stack/scripts/armada-disclosure-acceptance.py run on the warm snapshot has exit_code 0 and stdout_json hops_ok is true (hops H1, H2, H4, H5, H6 and H7 succeed).
stdout_json eoa2_usdc_delta is greater than 0, so the second account gains a positive USDC amount.
stdout_json eoa_distinct is true, so the two accounts differ.
stdout_json payout_note_owned is true, so the payout note belongs to the same wallet.
After the gate exits, no disclosure deployment runs and the deployment directory is gone.

goal: Add a gate job that runs the disclosure hops check on the warm snapshot and always cleans up the fixturenet.
acceptance_criteria: The disclosure hops gate script is present in the repository.
The gate script refers to the warm snapshot when it stands up the fixturenet.
The gate script does not run a cold build of the fixturenet.
The gate script sets a trap that runs on EXIT.
The gate script deletes the deployment directory with rm -rf.
Running the disclosure acceptance checker on the warm snapshot ends with success and reports that all hops succeeded.
The checker reports that the second account gained a positive USDC amount.
The checker reports that the two accounts are different.
The checker reports that the payout note belongs to the same wallet.
The checker reports a package file path that is not empty.
After the whole gate has run and exited, the gate reports that no disclosure deployment is running and the deployment directory is gone.
